title: Dotfiles: a shell setup in one script

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New machine, same terminal you love, in a single command. That's the idea behind Antoine's dotfiles.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the installer actually do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It manages packages, configuration files and upstream projects, so a fresh machine ends up with his shell and editor setup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does it only work on one Linux flavour?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. It supports apt, dnf and pacman, so it covers several distributions. And it's idempotent, meaning you can run it again safely and it only does what's missing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Modular Zsh and Vim setups, all in shell scripts under the MIT license. The written page has the layout.
